edge_board.description: Israel's Tel Aviv Flight Information Region has undergone repeated temporary closures and reopenings in 2026 tied to US-Israeli strikes on Iranian targets and subsequent Iranian missile-drone retaliations, with additional brief shutdowns following Houthi intercepts. As of mid-August the airspace remains open for civilian operations, though EASA and other regulators maintain elevated-risk advisories citing potential escalation from Hezbollah or other proxies amid the breakdown of the US-Iran ceasefire and renewed activity near the Strait of Hormuz. Market-implied probabilities reflect trader assessment that any near-term closure would likely be short-duration and triggered by specific incoming threats rather than a sustained shutdown, with resolution depending on verified flight suspensions at Ben Gurion or across the FIR. Key near-term catalysts include ongoing diplomatic or military developments in the Iran-Israel corridor that could prompt fresh alerts.
edge_board.question: Israel closes its airspace by August 15?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israel initiates a major closure of its airspace by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or complete suspension of commercial aviation across the entirety of Israeli civilian airspace or a region encompassing a majority of Israeli civilian airspace, including commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from that airspace. A qualifying closure must apply generally to all flights across Israel or a qualifying subset of Israeli airspace. Limited cancellations, delays, temporary ground stops or isolated regional closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain pre-approved flights may be permitted).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, flight suspensions, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Israel will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israeli aviation authorities; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

edge_board.description: Ongoing U.S.-Iran tensions and recent vessel attacks have kept Strait of Hormuz traffic at a fraction of normal levels since the February 2026 escalation, with only a handful of transits recorded in mid-August amid the reinstated U.S. naval blockade. This chokepoint normally carries roughly one-quarter of global oil flows, so sustained disruption has elevated energy prices, raised tanker insurance rates, and contributed to volatility in crude benchmarks and related equities. Iran-Oman talks on safe-passage arrangements are in advanced stages, with potential for a near-term agreement that could ease flows, though renewed attacks or enforcement actions remain key swing factors for market-implied probabilities. Traders are monitoring daily vessel data and diplomatic signals for shifts in the risk premium.
edge_board.question: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by August 31?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and August 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for August 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after the date on which such data is first released to allow for corrections. Data integrity issues refer only to clerical or other similar errors in the underlying data, and do not include cases where IMF Portwatch differs from alternative sources.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

edge_board.description: Traders assign a 96% probability to no Chinese invasion of Taiwan by December 31, 2026, reflecting the compressed timeframe and absence of observable large-scale amphibious mobilization. Recent months show continued gray-zone pressure through PLA live-fire drills in the Taiwan Strait and routine air and naval activity, alongside Taiwan’s annual Han Kuang exercises emphasizing reservist integration and supply resilience. Beijing’s approach favors sustained coercion short of war, including diplomatic outreach to Taiwan’s opposition ahead of future elections. Large-scale invasion preparations typically require visible logistics, naval deployments, and force posture shifts spanning many months, none of which have materialized. While a sudden miscalculation or unforeseen escalation remains possible in principle, the current pattern of events and structural constraints continue to support the market consensus.
edge_board.question: Will China invade Taiwan by end of 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of the Republic of China (Taiwan) by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Territory under the administration of the Republic of China including any inhabited islands will qualify, however uninhabited islands will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be will be official confirmation by China, Taiwan, the United Nations, or any permanent member of the UN Security Council, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.
